Neither the setting nor the check is needed. `services.fstrim.enable` defaults to `true` in nixpkgs: `nixos/modules/services/misc/fstrim.nix` declares `lib.mkEnableOption "periodic SSD TRIM…" // { default = true; }`. Nothing in the repository sets or overrides `fstrim` (grep of the repository, excluding openspec/logs/docs/notes, found no matches), so every NixOS host already has it on.

If the user still wants a guard against someone setting it to false later, the repository's ladder puts it on rung 1, not in a new standalone check:
- Edit a NixOS module beside the judge to register `fleetObligations.<key> = { classes = [ "nixos" ]; failures = name: hostConfig: lib.optional (!hostConfig.services.fstrim.enable) "…"; }`. This follows `lib/fleet-obligations.nix`, with `darwin/resolver-reload.nix` as the example.
- Add `<key>` to the literal `registeredObligations` list in `modules/checks/machines.nix`.
- Create `modules/checks/<name>-obligations.nix` holding a `flake.lib.mkJudgeCheck` over fixtures. It must include a failing negative-control case with its expected failure count, and a `testSizes.checks.<system>.<name>` entry (`class = "medium"; measured = false;` if unmeasured).

That check would live on `x86_64-linux`, the system of all the NixOS hosts in `machines.nix`. Its attribute name must be a literal, and its source must be no wider than what it reads.

Only if the fact must also hold on a `checked = false` host (scheelite) would it become a rung-2 standalone check in `modules/checks/`. That check would carry the same literal name, size class and negative control.

RULE: Check a fact on the cheapest rung that can observe its failure. A fact about one configuration's values is a fleet obligation judged in the machine checks. Also: "Before adding a setting and a check for 'every host', read the option's default: a setting nixpkgs or nix-darwin already turns on needs neither." Stated in `modules/checks/README.md`.
